newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Corp, union reach pact on refineries.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Corp, union reach pact on refineries.

text.p: Tosco Corp and the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) said on Saturday they had reached an agreement on a new five-year labour contract for four California refineries.
Tosco is buying the four refineries from Unocal Corp along with other related facilities. Tosco said it expects to close the purchase at midnight on March 31.
The deal includes the Wilmington refinery, a nearby refinery in Carson, another in Rodeo east of San Francisco and one in Santa Maria, between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Tosco's contract negotiations with the union had stalled last week, but company and union officials said on Monday that they had reached a tentative agreement.
On Saturday, Tosco and OCAW officials said union members at the four refineries had approved the contract.
"The membership ratified the contract," Tosco spokeswoman Linda Saltzman said. "Production has been and will continue uninterrupted."
Union officials, who had threatened to strike, welcomed the agreement.

"We're looking forward to getting beyond this," said Howard Spencer, president of OCAW Local 1-326, which represents union members at the Rodeo plant east of San Francisco. The OCAW represents about 900 workers at the four refineries. "The contract was well accepted across the board."
However, Spencer said he and other union leaders were concerned about Tosco's plan to cut the workforce at the plants.

Tosco said it did not extend offers to an estimated 15 percent of the 1,400 Unocal employees at the four refineries and other facilities. Some of the workers accepted positions elsewhere within Unocal, others accepted severance packages or retired early, Saltzman said.
Details of the new contract were not immediately available.
